typedef enum ZydisPrefixType_
{
    /**
     * The prefix is ignored by the instruction.
     *
     * This applies to all prefixes that are not accepted by the instruction in general or the
     * ones that are overwritten by a prefix of the same group closer to the instruction opcode.
     */
    ZYDIS_PREFIX_TYPE_IGNORED,
    /**
     * The prefix is effectively used by the instruction.
     */
    ZYDIS_PREFIX_TYPE_EFFECTIVE,
    /**
     * The prefix is used as a mandatory prefix.
     *
     * A mandatory prefix is interpreted as an opcode extension and has no further effect on the
     * instruction.
     */

    /**
     * Maximum value of this enum.
     */

Breakdown of the REX2 prefix fields and its byte offset within the instruction.
Breakdown of the AMD XOP prefix fields and its offset.
Breakdown of the VEX prefix fields, with offset and total prefix size.
Breakdown of the EVEX prefix fields and its byte offset including EVEX-specific controls (z, L/L2, b, aaa, etc.).
Breakdown of the MVEX prefix fields and its offset; includes KNC/MVEX-specific controls.
Holds AVX/AVX-512/KNC-specific decoded properties such as vector length, masking, broadcast, rounding, swizzle, conversion, SAE and eviction hint.

High-level metadata about the instruction such as category, ISA set/extension, branch type, and exception class.
Low-level breakdown of raw instruction encoding: legacy prefixes, REX/REX2/XOP/VEX/EVEX/MVEX unions, ModRM, SIB, displacement, and immediates with offsets and sizes.
Top-level result of decoding an instruction: mnemonic, lengths, widths, encoding, attributes, operand counts, flag effects, AVX/APX extensions, meta and raw encoding details.
Opaque decoder context preserving intermediate state for decoding phases of the same instruction. Marked private/unstable; fields are internal caches and helpers.

Aggregates commonly used information about a decoded instruction, including runtime address, machine-readable decode info and operands, and a preformatted text string. Filled by ZydisDisassembleIntel/ATT. Destruction/ownership: plain POD, no special lifetime; caller provides storage. Size of text buffer is fixed (96 bytes).

functions.name: ZydisGetVersion
functions.signature: ZyanU64 ZydisGetVersion(void);
functions.description: Returns the Zydis library version as a 64-bit packed value. Typical usage is to call this at runtime and extract major/minor/patch/build parts using the ZYDIS_VERSION_* helper macros defined in this header. No initialization or context is required.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should interpret the returned 64-bit value using the ZYDIS_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH/BUILD macros to obtain individual components.
Return value is a raw integer; there is no error reporting via this function.

functions.name: ZydisIsFeatureEnabled
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisIsFeatureEnabled(ZydisFeature feature);
functions.description: Checks whether a given Zydis feature (decoder, encoder, formatter, AVX-512, KNC, segment, etc.) is enabled in the current library build. Returns ZYAN_STATUS_TRUE if enabled, ZYAN_STATUS_FALSE if disabled, or another ZyanStatus error code if an error occurs. Use this to gate code paths that depend on optional build-time features.
requirements: feature must be a valid ZydisFeature value (between 0 and ZYDIS_FEATURE_MAX_VALUE inclusive).
Caller must handle the return ZyanStatus: expect ZYAN_STATUS_TRUE/ZYAN_STATUS_FALSE for the check result, but also handle other error codes.
No explicit initialization or state is required by this function (based on the header); thread-safety and additional side effects are unknown.

functions.name: ZydisDecoderInit
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDecoderInit(ZydisDecoder* decoder, ZydisMachineMode machine_mode, ZydisStackWidth stack_width);
functions.description: Initializes a ZydisDecoder instance for a given machine mode and stack width. Call this before any decoding functions. Returns a ZyanStatus indicating success or failure.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for a ZydisDecoder.
decoder must be initialized via this function before being used with other Zydis decoding APIs.
machine_mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode value.
stack_width must be a valid ZydisStackWidth value.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: ZydisDecoderEnableMode
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDecoderEnableMode(ZydisDecoder* decoder, ZydisDecoderMode mode, ZyanBool enabled);
functions.description: Enables or disables a specific decoder mode on an initialized decoder (e.g., AMD branches, APX, etc.). Use to tweak decoding semantics before decoding instructions.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisDecoder.
mode must be a valid ZydisDecoderMode value.
enabled must be ZYAN_TRUE to enable or ZYAN_FALSE to disable the mode.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: ZydisDecoderDecodeFull
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDecoderDecodeFull(const ZydisDecoder* decoder, const void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, ZydisDecodedOperand operands[ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT]);
functions.description: Convenience routine that decodes an instruction and all of its operands in a single call. Populates instruction with full details and writes up to ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT operands (excess entries are zeroed). Not available in MINIMAL mode.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisDecoder.
Function is not available in MINIMAL mode; do not call when ZYDIS_DECODER_MODE_MINIMAL is enabled.
buffer must be a valid pointer to at least length bytes; length may exceed actual instruction size and is used to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
length must correctly reflect the accessible size of buffer to avoid OOB reads.
instruction must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable ZydisDecodedInstruction storage.
operands must point to writable storage for ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT ZydisDecodedOperand entries; the caller may read instruction.operand_count to know how many were decoded (others are zeroed).
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction(const ZydisDecoder* decoder, ZydisDecoderContext* context, const void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction);
functions.description: Decodes an instruction from the given byte buffer and fills the instruction structure with details. Optionally produces a decoder context for subsequent operand decoding via ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisDecoder.
buffer must be a valid pointer to at least length bytes; length may exceed the actual instruction size and is used to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
length must correctly reflect the accessible size of buffer to avoid OOB reads.
instruction must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable ZydisDecodedInstruction storage.

context may be ZYAN_NULL if operand decoding is not needed; if operand decoding will follow, context must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable ZydisDecoderContext that is preserved and passed unchanged to ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands for the same instruction.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDecoderDecodeOperands(const ZydisDecoder* decoder, const ZydisDecoderContext* context, const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, ZydisDecodedOperand* operands, ZyanU8 operand_count);
functions.description: Decodes operands for a previously decoded instruction. Writes up to operand_count operands into the provided array. Fails if operand_count exceeds instruction.operand_count. Not available in MINIMAL mode.
requirements: decoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisDecoder.
Function is not available in MINIMAL mode; do not call when ZYDIS_DECODER_MODE_MINIMAL is enabled.
context must be a valid, non-null pointer to the ZydisDecoderContext produced by the matching ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction call for the same instruction.
instruction must be a valid, non-null pointer to the corresponding ZydisDecodedInstruction previously returned by ZydisDecoderDecodeInstruction.
If operand_count is 0, no operands will be decoded and operands may be ZYAN_NULL.
If operand_count > 0, operands must point to writable storage for at least operand_count ZydisDecodedOperand entries.
operand_count must be less than or equal to instruction.operand_count; otherwise the function fails.

For allocating operands, use sizes that accommodate ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT or ZYDIS_MAX_OPERAND_COUNT_VISIBLE to ensure buffers are always sufficient; when decoding for a specific instruction, ensure the buffer can hold instruction.operand_count or instruction.operand_count_visible as appropriate.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: ZydisDisassembleIntel
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDisassembleIntel(ZydisMachineMode machine_mode, ZyanU64 runtime_address, const void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZydisDisassembledInstruction* instruction);
functions.description: Disassembles a single instruction from the given buffer and formats it to a human-readable string using Intel syntax, filling a ZydisDisassembledInstruction with decoded info, operands, and formatted text. Intended as a convenience one-shot that internally performs decoder and formatter setup and decoding. Use when you need a straightforward way to decode/format one instruction without manually driving the decoder/formatter.
requirements: machine_mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode corresponding to the intended decoding mode (e.g., ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LONG_64 or ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LEGACY_32).
runtime_address is the assumed program counter for the instruction (RIP/EIP); provide the effective address to ensure correct decoding/formatting of RIP-relative and similar instructions.
buffer must point to at least length bytes of readable memory containing the instruction stream to decode; the function will not read past length bytes.
length must be the size (in bytes) of the accessible region starting at buffer; it may exceed the actual instruction size and is only used to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
instruction must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a ZydisDisassembledInstruction; it can be uninitialized on entry and may be reused across calls.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus and only use the contents of instruction if the status indicates success.

functions.name: ZydisDisassembleATT
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisDisassembleATT(ZydisMachineMode machine_mode, ZyanU64 runtime_address, const void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZydisDisassembledInstruction* instruction);
functions.description: Disassembles a single instruction from the given buffer and formats it to a human-readable string using AT&T syntax, filling a ZydisDisassembledInstruction with decoded info, operands, and formatted text. Convenience one-shot wrapper that internally sets up decoding and formatting.
requirements: machine_mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode corresponding to the intended decoding mode (e.g., ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LONG_64 or ZYDIS_MACHINE_MODE_LEGACY_32).
runtime_address is the assumed program counter for the instruction (RIP/EIP); provide the effective address to ensure correct decoding/formatting of RIP-relative and similar instructions.
buffer must point to at least length bytes of readable memory containing the instruction stream to decode; the function will not read past length bytes.
length must be the size (in bytes) of the accessible region starting at buffer; it may exceed the actual instruction size and is only used to prevent out-of-bounds reads.
instruction must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a ZydisDisassembledInstruction; it can be uninitialized on entry and may be reused across calls.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus and only use the contents of instruction if the status indicates success.

functions.name: ZydisEncoderEncodeInstruction
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisEncoderEncodeInstruction(const ZydisEncoderRequest* request, void* buffer, ZyanUSize* length);
functions.description: Encodes a single instruction described by the provided ZydisEncoderRequest into the given buffer. On entry, *length must contain the output buffer capacity in bytes; on success, it is updated with the encoded instruction size. Use this to turn a machine-mode/mnemonic/operands description into machine code bytes.
requirements: request must be a non-null pointer to a properly initialized ZydisEncoderRequest describing the instruction.
request->operand_count must not exceed ZYDIS_ENCODER_MAX_OPERANDS (5).
Any operands referenced by request->operands must be consistent with the instruction and contain valid types/values (e.g., valid registers, scale, displacement semantics as documented).
buffer must be non-null and point to writable memory of at least *length bytes on input.
length must be non-null; on input, *length specifies the size of buffer in bytes; on success, *length receives the number of bytes written.
If using absolute memory addresses (mem operand with only displacement), consider address_size_hint semantics; displacement is treated as a 64-bit signed integer.
EVEX/MVEX feature fields (broadcast/rounding/sae/etc.) must be set only when applicable to the target instruction; otherwise default/disabled values should be used.

functions.name: ZydisEncoderEncodeInstructionAbsolute
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisEncoderEncodeInstructionAbsolute(ZydisEncoderRequest* request, void* buffer, ZyanUSize* length, ZyanU64 runtime_address);
functions.description: Encodes a single instruction using absolute addresses in the request instead of RIP/EIP-relative values. The function predicts the final instruction length, computes the correct relative immediates from the provided absolute targets and runtime_address, and writes those relative values back into the request. On success, buffer receives the encoded bytes and *length the encoded size.
requirements: request must be a non-null pointer to a ZydisEncoderRequest and will be modified by the function (relative operands written back).
Absolute address values must be provided in the request where applicable (e.g., branch targets as absolute addresses rather than relative).
runtime_address must be the runtime address (instruction pointer) where the encoded instruction will reside.
buffer must be non-null and point to writable memory of at least *length bytes on input.
length must be non-null; on input, *length is the available buffer size; on success, *length receives the number of bytes written.
request->operand_count must not exceed ZYDIS_ENCODER_MAX_OPERANDS (5).
EVEX/MVEX feature fields should be set only when applicable to the instruction; otherwise use defaults.

functions.name: ZydisEncoderDecodedInstructionToEncoderRequest
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisEncoderDecodedInstructionToEncoderRequest(const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operands, ZyanU8 operand_count_visible, ZydisEncoderRequest* request);
functions.description: Converts a decoded instruction (and its decoded operands) into a ZydisEncoderRequest suitable for re-encoding with ZydisEncoderEncodeInstruction. The conversion performs minimal sanity checks; malformed inputs may yield a request that is not accepted by the encoder.
requirements: instruction must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction.
operands must point to an array containing at least operand_count_visible entries when operand_count_visible > 0; may be null if operand_count_visible is 0.
operand_count_visible must match the number of visible (explicit) operands of the decoded instruction.
request must be a non-null pointer to writable storage that will receive the generated encoder request.
Callers must not assume the produced request is always encodable; additional validation or an encode attempt is required to confirm.

functions.name: ZydisEncoderNopFill
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisEncoderNopFill(void* buffer, ZyanUSize length);
functions.description: Fills the provided buffer with a sequence of NOP instructions, choosing the longest possible multi-byte encodings to cover the given length. Useful for padding code with efficiently decodable NOPs.
requirements: buffer must be non-null and point to writable memory of at least length bytes.
length specifies the exact number of bytes to fill; if zero, no bytes are written (status behavior for zero length is implementation-defined/unknown).
The function does not take a machine mode parameter; any mode-specific behavior or NOP form selection beyond the header description is unknown.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterInit
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterInit(ZydisFormatter* formatter, ZydisFormatterStyle style);
functions.description: Initializes a ZydisFormatter instance with the specified base style (AT&T, Intel, or Intel MASM). Must be called before using the formatter for formatting/tokenizing. Returns a zyan status code indicating success or failure.
requirements: formatter must point to a valid ZydisFormatter storage location (caller-allocated).
style must be a valid ZydisFormatterStyle value (e.g., ZYDIS_FORMATTER_STYLE_ATT, ZYDIS_FORMATTER_STYLE_INTEL, ZYDIS_FORMATTER_STYLE_INTEL_MASM).
Callers should check the returned ZyanStatus for success before using the formatter.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterSetProperty
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterSetProperty(ZydisFormatter* formatter, ZydisFormatterProperty property, ZyanUPointer value);
functions.description: Sets a configurable property on an initialized ZydisFormatter (e.g., number bases, signedness, padding, case, prefixes/suffixes). Returns ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION if the property cannot be changed for the current formatter style.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
property must be a valid ZydisFormatterProperty constant.

value must be appropriate for the property being set (e.g., boolean properties expect ZYAN_TRUE/ZYAN_FALSE; numeric base expects a ZydisNumericBase; signedness expects a ZydisSignedness; padding expects a ZydisPadding; string prefix/suffix properties expect a pointer to a null-terminated C-string up to length 10 or ZYAN_NULL).
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus and handle ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION when a property is not applicable to the current style.
Strings passed via prefix/suffix properties are deep-copied; the input pointer need only be valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterSetHook
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterSetHook(ZydisFormatter* formatter, ZydisFormatterFunction type, const void** callback);
functions.description: Replaces a formatter hook with a custom callback and/or retrieves the currently used function for the given hook type. If callback points to a NULL value on entry, the function only retrieves the current callback without replacing it. Returns ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION if the hook cannot be replaced for the current style.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
type must be a valid ZydisFormatterFunction value.
callback must point to a variable holding the incoming replacement pointer and that receives the previously used function pointer on success.
To only query the currently installed hook without replacing it, set *callback to ZYAN_NULL before the call.
Callers must ensure the function pointer they install has the correct prototype for the selected type (e.g., ZydisFormatterFunc, ZydisFormatterRegisterFunc, or ZydisFormatterDecoratorFunc).
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus and handle ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION when a hook is not replaceable for the current style.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterFormatInstruction
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterFormatInstruction(const ZydisFormatter* formatter, const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operands, ZyanU8 operand_count, char* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZyanU64 runtime_address, void* user_data);
functions.description: Formats a previously decoded instruction (and its operands) into human-readable text and writes it to a character buffer. The result follows the active formatter style and properties. runtime_address controls absolute vs. relative address printing (use ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE for relative). Returns a zyan status code.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
instruction must point to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by Zydis decoding.
operands must point to the decoded operands array corresponding to instruction.
operand_count must be >= instruction->operand_count_visible.
buffer must point to writable memory for at least length characters (including space for the terminating null if the implementation writes one).
length specifies the buffer capacity in characters.
runtime_address may be ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE to force relative addressing; otherwise it should be the runtime address of the instruction.
user_data may be ZYAN_NULL; if provided, it is made available to custom formatter callbacks.
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus for success.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterFormatOperand
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterFormatOperand(const ZydisFormatter* formatter, const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operand, char* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZyanU64 runtime_address, void* user_data);
functions.description: Formats a single operand of a previously decoded instruction into human-readable text and writes it to a character buffer. Use the instruction-wide API to format a complete instruction. runtime_address controls absolute vs. relative address printing (use ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE for relative). Returns a zyan status code.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
instruction must point to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by Zydis decoding.
operand must point to the ZydisDecodedOperand to be formatted and belong to instruction.
buffer must point to writable memory for at least length characters.
length specifies the buffer capacity in characters.
runtime_address may be ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE to force relative addressing; otherwise it should be the runtime address of the instruction.
user_data may be ZYAN_NULL; if provided, it is made available to custom formatter callbacks.
For formatting a full instruction string, prefer ZydisFormatterFormatInstruction.
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus for success.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterTokenizeInstruction
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterTokenizeInstruction(const ZydisFormatter* formatter, const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operands, ZyanU8 operand_count, void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZyanU64 runtime_address, ZydisFormatterTokenConst** token, void* user_data);
functions.description: Tokenizes a decoded instruction into a sequence of formatter tokens written into a caller-provided buffer, and returns a pointer to the first token. Enables structured consumption of the disassembly (mnemonic, registers, immediates, etc.). length is in bytes. runtime_address controls absolute vs. relative address printing (use ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE for relative). Returns a zyan status code.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
instruction must point to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by Zydis decoding.
operands must point to the decoded operands array corresponding to instruction.
operand_count must be >= instruction->operand_count_visible.
buffer must point to writable memory for at least length bytes suitable for storing the token stream.
length specifies the buffer capacity in bytes.
token must point to a variable that will receive a pointer to the first token in the buffer.
runtime_address may be ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE to force relative addressing; otherwise it should be the runtime address of the instruction.
user_data may be ZYAN_NULL; if provided, it is made available to custom formatter callbacks.
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus for success.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterTokenizeOperand
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterTokenizeOperand(const ZydisFormatter* formatter, const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operand, void* buffer, ZyanUSize length, ZyanU64 runtime_address, ZydisFormatterTokenConst** token, void* user_data);
functions.description: Tokenizes a single operand of a decoded instruction into formatter tokens written into a caller-provided buffer, and returns a pointer to the first token. Use the instruction-wide API to tokenize a full instruction. length is in bytes. runtime_address controls absolute vs. relative address printing (use ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE for relative). Returns a zyan status code.
requirements: formatter must point to an initialized ZydisFormatter.
instruction must point to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by Zydis decoding.
operand must point to the ZydisDecodedOperand to be tokenized and belong to instruction.
buffer must point to writable memory for at least length bytes suitable for storing the token stream.
length specifies the buffer capacity in bytes.
token must point to a variable that will receive a pointer to the first token in the buffer.
runtime_address may be ZYDIS_RUNTIME_ADDRESS_NONE to force relative addressing; otherwise it should be the runtime address of the instruction.
user_data may be ZYAN_NULL; if provided, it is made available to custom formatter callbacks.
For tokenizing a full instruction, prefer ZydisFormatterTokenizeInstruction.
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus for success.

functions.name: ZydisFormatterTokenGetValue
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterTokenGetValue(const ZydisFormatterToken* token, ZydisTokenType* type, ZyanConstCharPointer* value)
functions.description: Returns the token type and a pointer to the token’s string value for the given formatter token. Use this to inspect tokens produced by the formatter/token buffer. The returned value pointer refers to internal storage owned by the token stream.
requirements: token must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisFormatterToken within a live token list
type must be non-null and will be written with the token type
value must be non-null and will receive a pointer to the token’s literal string
The returned value pointer is only valid while the underlying token stream/buffer remains alive; do not free or modify it
Callers must check the returned ZyanStatus and handle errors

functions.name: ZydisFormatterTokenNext
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterTokenNext(ZydisFormatterTokenConst** token)
functions.description: Advances to and returns the next token linked to the current one. Pass a pointer to a token pointer; on success, the pointer is updated to the next token.
requirements: token must be non-null and must point to a valid token pointer; *token must reference a valid token in a token list produced by the formatter
On success, *token is set to the next token; callers must check the returned ZyanStatus to detect end-of-list or errors
The token list must remain valid for the duration of iteration (do not destroy/overwrite the buffer while iterating)

functions.name: ZydisFormatterBufferGetToken
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterBufferGetToken(const ZydisFormatterBuffer* buffer, ZydisFormatterTokenConst** token)
functions.description: Retrieves the current (most recently added) token from the formatter buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisFormatterBuffer
token must be non-null and will receive the pointer to the current token
The buffer must contain at least one token; otherwise the function returns ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION
Callers must check and handle the returned ZyanStatus
The returned token pointer remains valid only while the buffer and its token list remain alive

functions.name: ZydisFormatterBufferGetString
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterBufferGetString(ZydisFormatterBuffer* buffer, ZyanString** string)
functions.description: Returns the ZyanString instance associated with the buffer. The string always refers to the literal value of the current (most recently added) token and remains valid until the buffer is destroyed. The instance is automatically updated when the buffer changes.
requirements: buffer must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisFormatterBuffer
string must be non-null and will receive the pointer to the associated ZyanString
The buffer must contain at least one token; otherwise the function returns ZYAN_STATUS_INVALID_OPERATION
Do not free or modify internal storage of the returned ZyanString; its lifetime is tied to the buffer
Callers must check and handle the returned ZyanStatus

functions.name: ZydisFormatterBufferAppend
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterBufferAppend(ZydisFormatterBuffer* buffer, ZydisTokenType type)
functions.description: Appends a new token of the specified type to the formatter buffer. On success, the buffer’s associated ZyanString (retrieved via ZydisFormatterBufferGetString) is automatically updated to refer to the new token’s literal value.
requirements: buffer must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisFormatterBuffer
type must be a valid token type (built-in constants or user-defined starting at ZYDIS_TOKEN_USER)
Callers must check and handle the returned ZyanStatus
Sufficient remaining capacity must exist in the buffer for the new token (otherwise the function may fail)
Do not assume any specific content in the associated ZyanString beyond it referencing the newly appended token’s literal value

functions.name: ZydisFormatterBufferRemember
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterBufferRemember(const ZydisFormatterBuffer* buffer, ZyanUPointer* state)
functions.description: Takes a snapshot of the buffer’s state for later restoration. The snapshot is stored inside the buffer and becomes invalid once the buffer is overwritten or destroyed.
requirements: buffer must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisFormatterBuffer
state must be non-null and will receive the opaque snapshot value
The saved snapshot is only valid while the originating buffer remains alive and unoverwritten
Callers must check and handle the returned ZyanStatus

functions.name: ZydisFormatterBufferRestore
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisFormatterBufferRestore(ZydisFormatterBuffer* buffer, ZyanUPointer state)
functions.description: Restores a previously saved buffer state obtained via ZydisFormatterBufferRemember. All tokens added after the snapshot are removed. The function does not restore any string content, but the associated ZyanString is automatically updated to reflect the restored state.
requirements: buffer must be a non-null pointer to an initialized ZydisFormatterBuffer
state must be a snapshot previously obtained from the same buffer via ZydisFormatterBufferRemember
Restoration removes all tokens added after the snapshot; no string content is restored
Callers must check and handle the returned ZyanStatus
Do not use snapshots after the buffer has been overwritten or destroyed

functions.name: ZydisCategoryGetString
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT const char* ZydisCategoryGetString(ZydisInstructionCategory category);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable C string for the given ZydisInstructionCategory value. Use it to obtain the textual instruction category name (e.g., for logging or formatting). Returns ZYAN_NULL if category is invalid. The returned pointer refers to an internal static string (inferred; not explicitly documented) and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: category must be a valid ZydisInstructionCategory value to receive a non-null result
the caller must handle a possible ZYAN_NULL return before dereferencing or using the string
the returned pointer must not be freed by the caller (inferred from const char* return to internal data)
the returned string should be treated as read-only (const)

functions.name: ZydisISASetGetString
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT const char* ZydisISASetGetString(ZydisISASet isa_set);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable C string for the given ZydisISASet value. Use it to obtain the textual ISA set name. Returns ZYAN_NULL if isa_set is invalid. The returned pointer is expected to reference internal storage and must not be modified or freed (inferred; not explicitly documented).
requirements: isa_set must be a valid ZydisISASet value to receive a non-null result
the caller must check for a possible ZYAN_NULL result before using the string
the returned pointer must not be freed by the caller (inferred)
the returned string should be treated as read-only (const)

functions.name: ZydisISAExtGetString
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT const char* ZydisISAExtGetString(ZydisISAExt isa_ext);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable C string for the given ZydisISAExt value. Use it to obtain the textual ISA extension name. Returns ZYAN_NULL if isa_ext is invalid. The returned pointer is expected to reference internal storage and must not be modified or freed (inferred; not explicitly documented).
requirements: isa_ext must be a valid ZydisISAExt value to receive a non-null result
the caller must handle a possible ZYAN_NULL return before using the string
the returned pointer must not be freed by the caller (inferred)
the returned string should be treated as read-only (const)

functions.name: ZydisMnemonicGetString
functions.signature: const char* ZydisMnemonicGetString(ZydisMnemonic mnemonic);
functions.description: Returns the textual mnemonic name for the given ZydisMnemonic value. Use this to map an instruction mnemonic enum to its canonical string. Returns NULL if the mnemonic is invalid or not recognized.
requirements: Argument mnemonic must be a ZydisMnemonic value; passing an invalid value will result in a NULL return.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
The returned pointer refers to read-only string data (const char*); the caller must not modify it.

functions.name: ZydisMnemonicGetStringWrapped
functions.signature: const ZydisShortString* ZydisMnemonicGetStringWrapped(ZydisMnemonic mnemonic);
functions.description: Returns the mnemonic name for the given ZydisMnemonic value wrapped in a ZydisShortString container. Returns NULL if the mnemonic is invalid. The buffer of the returned struct is guaranteed to be zero-terminated in this special case (as documented).
requirements: Argument mnemonic must be a ZydisMnemonic value; passing an invalid value will result in a NULL return.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before dereferencing.
The returned pointer refers to read-only data (const ZydisShortString*); the caller must not modify the underlying buffer.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterEncode
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZydisRegister ZydisRegisterEncode(ZydisRegisterClass register_class, ZyanU8 id);
functions.description: Returns the concrete ZydisRegister identified by a (register_class, id) tuple. Use to map a class-local index to the corresponding register enum (e.g., GPR32+id -> EAX/…); returns ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE for invalid inputs.
requirements: register_class must be a valid ZydisRegisterClass that supports id-based addressing (per library enums).
id must be within the valid range for the specified register_class; out-of-range or unsupported tuples yield ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE.
Callers must handle the case that ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE is returned for invalid parameters.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetId
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanI8 ZydisRegisterGetId(ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the class-local id of reg, suitable for pairing with its class to re-encode the register. Returns -1 if reg is invalid. Some registers may not have a meaningful id in their class (e.g., special cases), which is not explicitly documented here.
requirements: reg should be a valid ZydisRegister value that belongs to a class with id-addressable members.
Callers must check for a return value of -1 indicating an invalid parameter.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetClass
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZydisRegisterClass ZydisRegisterGetClass(ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the ZydisRegisterClass to which reg belongs. Useful to group registers or to derive (class,id) pairs together with ZydisRegisterGetId.
requirements: reg should be a valid ZydisRegister.
Behavior for invalid reg is not explicitly documented; callers should ensure reg is valid or handle implementation-defined results.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetWidth
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZydisRegisterWidth ZydisRegisterGetWidth(ZydisMachineMode mode, ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the width (in bits) of reg under the given machine mode. If the register is invalid for the active mode, returns ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE.
requirements: mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode corresponding to the intended decoding/encoding context.
reg must be a valid ZydisRegister; if reg is not valid in the given mode the function returns ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE.
Callers must check for a return value of ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE to detect invalid-for-mode registers.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetLargestEnclosing
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZydisRegister ZydisRegisterGetLargestEnclosing(ZydisMachineMode mode, ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the largest enclosing register for reg in the given machine mode (e.g., AL -> RAX in 64-bit mode). Returns ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE if reg is invalid for the mode.
requirements: mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode.
reg must be a valid ZydisRegister; if reg is not valid in the given mode the function returns ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE.
Callers must handle ZYDIS_REGISTER_NONE indicating that no enclosing register exists for the given mode/reg.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetString
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT const char* ZydisRegisterGetString(ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the canonical lowercase string name of reg (e.g., "rax"). Returns NULL if reg is invalid. Intended for display, logging, or formatting.
requirements: reg should be a valid ZydisRegister.
The returned pointer may be NULL; callers must check before use.
The returned string is const; callers must not modify or free it.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterGetStringWrapped
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT const ZydisShortString* ZydisRegisterGetStringWrapped(ZydisRegister reg);
functions.description: Returns the register name of reg wrapped in a ZydisShortString object. Returns NULL if reg is invalid. For this function, the buffer field of the returned struct is guaranteed to be zero-terminated.
requirements: reg should be a valid ZydisRegister.
The returned pointer may be NULL; callers must check before use.
The returned ZydisShortString pointer refers to immutable data; callers must not modify or free it.
Consumers may rely on the buffer being zero-terminated for this special case as documented.

functions.name: ZydisRegisterClassGetWidth
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZydisRegisterWidth ZydisRegisterClassGetWidth(ZydisMachineMode mode, ZydisRegisterClass register_class);
functions.description: Returns the bit-width of registers in register_class for the given machine mode (e.g., GPR32 -> 32). Useful for sizing decisions without specifying a particular register.
requirements: mode must be a valid ZydisMachineMode.
register_class must be a valid ZydisRegisterClass. Error/edge-case behavior for invalid inputs is not explicitly documented.

functions.name: ZydisGetInstructionSegments
functions.signature: ZyanStatus ZydisGetInstructionSegments(const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, ZydisInstructionSegments* segments);
functions.description: Returns the byte offsets and sizes of all logical segments (prefixes, opcode, ModRM, SIB, displacement, immediate, etc.) that make up a previously decoded instruction. Typical usage: decode an instruction with the Zydis decoder APIs to obtain a ZydisDecodedInstruction, then call this function to retrieve per-segment layout information for analysis, display, or tooling. On success, the segments struct is populated with count and per-segment entries; only the first count elements are valid. Returns a ZyanStatus indicating success or failure.
requirements: instruction must be a valid, non-null pointer to a ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by a Zydis decode function and must remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred from parameter type and typical Zydis usage).

segments must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory; on success, it will be filled with up to ZYDIS_MAX_INSTRUCTION_SEGMENT_COUNT entries (inferred from output parameter and struct definition).
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus and only read segments on success (common Zyan/Zydis convention).
Only the first segments->count entries in segments->segments are valid after a successful call (stated by struct semantics).
Do not assume more than ZYDIS_MAX_INSTRUCTION_SEGMENT_COUNT (9) segments will be produced (from the defined constant).

functions.name: ZydisCalcAbsoluteAddress
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisCalcAbsoluteAddress(const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operand, ZyanU64 runtime_address, ZyanU64* result_address);
functions.description: Computes the absolute target address for a specific operand of a decoded instruction. Use for operands that encode addresses relative to the instruction pointer (e.g., relative immediates in JMP/CALL) or memory operands using RIP/EIP-relative addressing, and for memory operands with absolute addresses where displacement truncation/zero-extension is required. Typical usage: decode an instruction, select the relevant operand from the decoded instruction, provide the runtime address of the instruction, and receive the computed absolute address in result_address. Returns a ZyanStatus indicating success or failure.
requirements: instruction must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by the decoder.
operand must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisDecodedOperand belonging to the provided instruction.
runtime_address must be the actual runtime address of the instruction corresponding to instruction; it is used for relative calculations.
result_address must be a non-null pointer to writable memory to receive the computed address.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus and only use result_address on success.
Intended for: IMM operands with relative address, MEM operands with RIP/EIP-relative address, and MEM operands with absolute addresses; using it for other operand kinds may fail or be nonsensical.

functions.name: ZydisCalcAbsoluteAddressEx
functions.signature: ZYDIS_EXPORT ZyanStatus ZydisCalcAbsoluteAddressEx(const ZydisDecodedInstruction* instruction, const ZydisDecodedOperand* operand, ZyanU64 runtime_address, const ZydisRegisterContext* register_context, ZyanU64* result_address);
functions.description: Computes the absolute target address for a specific operand of a decoded instruction, using an additional register context for operands whose effective address depends on runtime register values (e.g., base/index registers). Behaves like ZydisCalcAbsoluteAddress but consults register_context for register-dependent components. IP/EIP/RIP values from register_context are ignored in favor of runtime_address. Returns a ZyanStatus indicating success or failure.
requirements: instruction must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisDecodedInstruction produced by the decoder.
operand must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisDecodedOperand belonging to the provided instruction.
runtime_address must be the actual runtime address of the instruction; it supersedes IP/EIP/RIP in register_context for relative computations.
register_context must be a non-null pointer to a valid ZydisRegisterContext; fields other than IP/EIP/RIP are used to resolve register-dependent addressing.
result_address must be a non-null pointer to writable memory to receive the computed address.
Caller must check the returned ZyanStatus and only use result_address on success.

Intended for: IMM operands with relative address, MEM operands with RIP/EIP-relative address, and MEM/register-based operands requiring runtime register values; using it for other operand kinds may fail or be nonsensical.

data_types.description: An unstructured byte sequence with no required encoding or format. May contain any values from 0x00 to 0xFF. Used here as instruction bytes fed to the decoder/disassembler; length may be truncated by the fuzzer.
A short, null-terminated C string up to 10 characters in length, expected to contain printable ASCII text. Used for formatter prefix/suffix properties that accept user-provided strings.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: short ASCII string (<=10 bytes), NUL-terminated when used by C caller.
# Our generator returns bytes; fuzzer will pass it to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() usages, which
# in this stub are used for ZYDIS_FORMATTER_PROP_DEC_PREFIX. API copies up to 10 chars.
# We therefore generate interesting, valid ASCII strings of length 0..10 (excluding the
# terminating NUL; the harness typically appends NUL when converting bytes to std::string).

_PRINTABLE = (
    string.digits + string.ascii_letters + string.punctuation + " "
)

# Some hand-picked interesting tokens to exercise code paths (hex/dec styles, prefixes, etc.)
_INTERESTING: List[str] = [
    "",              # empty -> treated as no prefix
    "0x",            # common hex prefix
    "0X",            # upper-case variant
    "0",             # single digit
    "+",             # sign
    "-",             # negative sign
    "#",             # alternative base indicator (some assemblers)
    "h",             # MASM hex suffix style
    "0d",            # decimal hint
    "0b",            # binary-style prefix
    "$",             # some syntaxes use $ as hex
    "prefix",        # generic word
    "PRE",           # uppercase
    "_",             # underscore
    "::",            # punctuation
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(0, max_len)
    if n == 0:
        return ""
    # Mix: sometimes use digits/letters only, sometimes full printable set
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    else:
        alphabet = _PRINTABLE
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _choose_interesting(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer interesting samples, occasionally synthesize random
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        s = r.choice(_INTERESTING)
        # Maybe tweak by appending a small random suffix to stay <= 10
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            room = 10 - len(s)
            if room > 0:
                s += _rand_ascii(r, min(room, 3))
        return s[:10]
    return _rand_ascii(r, 10)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    s = _choose_interesting(r)
    # Ensure ASCII only and length <= 10
    s = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:10].decode('ascii')
    return s.encode('ascii')
